newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-April 25.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-April 25.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Friday morning:
** Prices of government securities end down on Thursday on fears the central bank would sell newly issued 10-year bonds at prices below current market rates, dealers say
** Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) forecasts a 28 percent fall in its 1997/98 (March-April) net and a production shortfall of nearly one million tonnes, the Financial Express says

** The borrowing cost of prime corporates has fallen by more than 150 basis points in the past week -- a direct result. of the freedom given to banks in making lending decisions in the credit policy this year, the Business Standard says

** Ernst & Young forecasts six percent gross domestic product growth for 1997/98, the same as the previous year. The global management consultant warns of continuing political instability affecting business and foreign investor confidence, the Business Standard says

** Former Finance Minister P. Chidambaram's regional Tamil Maanila Congress party is due to meet on April 27 to decide if it should reverse its decision keep out of the new United Front government of Prime Minister Inder Gujral
** Gujral's cabinet adopts 1997/98 budget which had been presented to parliament Chidambaram

** An official spokesman tells reporters the government looks forward to parliament adopting the budget, and will not discuss any amendments outside of parliament as the tax and spending plan was before lawmakers for their consideration
** India needs to do more to reform its economy and in particular to cut its big budget deficits, International Monetary Fund Managing Director Michel Camdessus says
He calls the country's overall public sector borrowing requirement of nine percent of gross domestic product "unsustainable"
** Calcutta Electric Supply Corp Ltd (CESC) will launch a $70 million 10-year FRN on April 28, lead manager ANZ Investment Bank says
The bond, maturing in May 2007, will be priced with a coupon of six-month Libor plus 150 basis points and a par issue price
** Bombay's benchmark share index .BSESN ends 23.27 points, or 0.61 percent down at 3805.72 on Thursday -- off the day's low of 3793.48
